title: Beyond the 956: Irma P. Hall, 'Soul Food' star and NAACP Image Award winner, dies at 91
excerpt: Irma P. Hall, the veteran actress best known as Big Mama in the 1997 film Soul Food, died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Dallas. She was 91. Her family announced her death on November 11.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Irma P. Hall, the veteran actress best known as Big Mama in the 1997 film Soul Food, died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Dallas. She was 91.

Her family announced her death on Wednesday, November 11. No cause of death was disclosed, and the family asked for privacy as it grieves. Her family said she died surrounded by her loved ones.

Born Irma Dolores Player on June 3, 1935, in Beaumont, Texas, Hall was raised in Chicago and later returned to Texas for college. She spent more than two decades teaching English and foreign languages in Dallas public schools before her acting career took off.

Hall was 60 when she broke through in A Family Thing (1996), alongside Robert Duvall and James Earl Jones. A year later, she played Mama Joseph, known to everyone as Big Mama, in Soul Food — the family matriarch whose Sunday dinners held a Chicago family together. The role won her an NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture, and she later reprised it in the Showtime television series.

In 2004, she starred opposite Tom Hanks in the Coen brothers’ comedy The Ladykillers, playing Marva Munson, a Bible-reading widow who rents a room to a group of criminals. Her performance earned her a Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival. Hanks paid tribute to her on Instagram, writing, “Irma P. Hall was a sheer joy… May her memory be eternal.”

Her other film credits included Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (1997), Beloved (1998), Patch Adams (1998), Collateral (2004) and Tyler Perry’s Meet the Browns (2008). On television, she appeared in Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, The Game, Chicago Fire and Hap and Leonard.

In its statement, her family called her “a beloved actress, author, poet, educator, and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career.” Details of funeral services and memorial tributes will be announced later, the family said.

Sources: Variety; ABC News; Los Angeles Sentinel.
